title: Design policy + delivery plan for immutable audit logging & WORM retention across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Provide a compliant, auditable, and tamper-evident audit logging system for admin actions, data access, and config changes with configurable retention (including WORM semantics) by customer region and deployment type (hosted, dedicated, private). This ticket covers the product requirements, acceptance criteria, trade-offs and rollout plan; engineering implementation tickets are tracked under ENG-3341 and ENG-3389. The solution must satisfy common regulatory needs (GDPR residency controls, UK/EU data residency, FedRAMP/SOC2 evidence generation) and provide automated evidence exports for audits.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a policy layer in Console to declare retention rules by scope (account, workspace, project) and residency region with optional WORM enforcement. 2) Wire audit events into an immutable append-only store: hosted: S3 Object Lock + KMS + signed manifests; dedicated/private: option to enable local WORM appliance or append-only PostgreSQL with LSN-backed signed checkpoints. 3) Cryptographic integrity: sign each batch of events with a per-account signing key (KMS/HSM) and maintain a Merkle tree root ledger for tamper-evidence. 4) Evidence automation: generate time-bounded attestations (ZIP with signed manifest, audit summary, hash index) accessible via Console and API for auditors with role-restricted downloads. 5) Retention enforcement and deletion: retention enforced server-side; expiry triggers archival workflow that produces final signed chain-of-custody record. 6) Expose immutable audit viewer in Console with filters (action, actor, resource, time, geo) and export hooks.
alternatives_considered: Write-once via DB-level append-only rows + periodic cold snapshots: lower infra complexity but harder to satisfy S3 WORM requirements and cross-region residency.
Rely solely on cloud provider access logs (CloudTrail/GCS Audit): less dev work but lacks granular config-change context and per-customer signing/retention control.
Use third-party compliance log provider (e.g., dedicated WORM service): faster to market but increases vendor-dependency, cost, and integration complexity for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: policy editor to configure retention period (days/years), WORM enable toggle, and residency selection per workspace.
Audit events: admin actions, config changes, access/grant events, token/credential rotations all recorded with request metadata and immutable sequence IDs.
Integrity: every exported evidence bundle includes signed manifest and a verifiable Merkle root consistent with stored events.
Retention enforcement: attempts to alter or delete protected records are rejected and logged; delete requests after retention period produce signed archival records.
Automated reporting: schedulable monthly audit package generation and on-demand investigator export via API; downloads restricted to auditor roles with 2FA requirement.
Private deployment parity: documented deployment recipe for enabling WORM semantics on-prem (OSS + recommended appliance), and required infra checks in install playbook.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Raman: Created initial ticket after legal requested explicit WORM retention and automated evidence exports for upcoming SOC2 re-audit.
2026-03-02 Miguel Ortiz: Drafted proposed solution and shared with Eng/Legal. Pulled ENG-3341 (append-only store) and ENG-3389 (evidence export pipeline).
2026-03-04 Legal (S. Patel): Confirmed that per-region residency + WORM suffices for primary audit scope; requested exportability in tamper-evident format and retention proof (signed manifests).

2026-03-06 Design review: UX needs inline policy validation and informative warnings when enabling WORM (irreversible within retention). Design spec PR: https://drive.redwoodinc/policyspecs/PM-4728-design-v1

2026-03-10 Eng sync (R. Chen): Raised implementation constraint: S3 Object Lock cannot be toggled off once enabled for a bucket; need migration plan for existing customers. Added ENG-3412 for migration assessment.
2026-03-12 Security (L. Nguyen): Recommended HSM-backed signing for hosted; for Dedicated/Private allow customer-managed keys (BYOK) or HW enclave. Also requested threat model and key-rotation doc.
2026-03-14 Miguel Ortiz: Updated acceptance criteria and added rollout plan; scheduled spike week for prototype (ENG-3341 spike).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Spike, 2 weeks): validate signing + Merkle packaging prototype, S3 Object Lock testbeds, and private deployment WORM recipe. (ENG-3341-SPK)
Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks): Console policy UI + hosted runbook using S3 Object Lock + KMS signing + evidence export API. Limited beta with 5 pilot customers.
Phase 2 (Parity & Dedicated, 8 weeks): Dedicated cluster option with managed WORM buckets, BYOK support, and migration tooling for existing accounts.
Phase 3 (Private/on-prem, 6 weeks): Publish install recipe for on-prem WORM appliance + signed manifests and optional offline attestation flow.
Phase 4 (Audit automation & docs): Automated scheduled packages, SOC2 evidence templates, and playbooks for auditors.
qa_notes: Test vectors: create synthetic sequence of admin actions, run through retention window, ensure pre-expiry immutability and post-expiry archival record exists.
Integrity test: modify a stored event byte and verify export fails verification via Merkle root mismatch.
Performance: measure 95th percentile latency for writes under batching vs direct write (metric threshold < 30ms added into SLOs).
Chaos: simulate region failover and ensure signed manifests and event ordering are preserved across replication.
